comments.body: Thanks - it seems that the validation for array API inputs is too strict: we should probably allow Python scalars here: https://github.com/google/jax/blob/1d26365e601528d4cb63ca9d39213248eb320adb/jax/experimental/array_api/_elementwise_functions.py#L25-L26

> Thanks - it seems that the validation for array API inputs is too strict: we should probably allow Python scalars here:

Hmm, are you sure that's enough?   If you produce scalars, it means that client code has to handle scalars, which often means wrapping return values in `jnp.asarray`.  Also, the [Array API spec](https://data-apis.org/array-api/latest/API_specification/generated/array_api.imag.html) says that `imag` returns an "array".  Doesn't that mean that the return value should be a `jax.Array`?

(That said, allowing scalars might have eliminated some wrapping I had to do, so that might also be a good idea.)

In general JAX code uses scalars and arrays interchangeably: for example, in jaxprs, compile-time constants are represented by scalars, not by JAX arrays. I suspect it would be very intrusive to try to change this.

Another aspect of this change: evenutally, when `jax.numpy` itself subsumes `jax.experimental.array_api`, the functions will accept scalar arguments, so this change makes the current temporary namespace more inline with how it will look in the future.

> In general JAX code uses scalars and arrays interchangeably: for example, in jaxprs, compile-time constants are represented by scalars, not by JAX arrays. I suspect it would be very intrusive to try to change this.

I understand that, but I think we're talking about different things.

Whether the library _accepts_ scalars in place of arrays is up to you.  That's not the issue.

The issue is what the Jax library _returns_.  As a user, I think we should be able to count on the return value being an array because that's what the spec promises.  Otherwise, Array API compliant code will not run with Jax.

If `x` is a Jax array, it should be possible to say: `x.imag.shape`.  Don't you agree?

If you don't want to follow the spec, then I think we should open an issue on the Array API tracker to change `imag` to return an array or scalar.

> The issue is what the Jax library returns

Understood: within traced code, `tracer.imag` returns a float `0.0` for a real-valued tracer, representing the fact that it's a constant that does not depend on any input value.

This is a bit of a tricky area: note that `x.imag` will always return an array if the input is an array (rather than something derived from a Python scalar).
```
In [2]: def f(x):
   ...:     print(type(x.imag))
   ...:     return x
   ...: 

In [3]: f(1.0)
<class 'float'>
Out[3]: 1.0

In [4]: jax.jit(f)(1.0)
<class 'float'>
Out[4]: Array(1., dtype=float32, weak_type=True)

In [5]: f(jnp.arange(4))
<class 'jaxlib.xla_extension.ArrayImpl'>
Out[5]: Array([0, 1, 2, 3], dtype=int32)

In [6]: jax.jit(f)(jnp.arange(4))
<class 'jax._src.interpreters.partial_eval.DynamicJaxprTracer'>
Out[6]: Array([0, 1, 2, 3], dtype=int32)
```
`jnp.array(0.0)` is kind of a strange thing: it's essentially JAX's representation of a float scalar, signified by `weak_type=True`. This lets us trace functions with scalar arguments so that they'll have the same semantics as a non-traced version of the function. This does lead to weird corner cases, but my experience is that changing those corner cases often leads to other, deeper errors.

It may be worth exploring whether we can make `x.imag` return something with a `shape` attribute, though.

> Changing this will be a very intrusive change, and may not be easy to do.

Okay, glad we're on the same page :smile:   It's unfortunate that's a difficult change, but I guess it has to do with declaring that the value is constant?

Regarding your last comment, yeah I was just trying various things like that.  I understand your point.  From the outside, it is a bit odd that scalar arrays are so fundamentally different from non-scalar arrays.

Would it be possible to use `np.empty((), dtype=float0` in place of 0.0?  Perhaps this can be solved in tandem with https://github.com/google/jax/issues/20620?
`float0` is an autodiff thing; this is unrelated.

Strangely enough, all of this scalar array weirdness comes from the fact that we want `x + 1` to have the same dtype as `x`. It's hard to change these things without affecting those promotion semantics.
Okay, I thought it was just a way to represent a constant zero, which seems to be the motivation for using 0.0 instead of `jnp.zeros(())` ?  Thanks for correcting me.

> Okay, I thought it was just a way to represent a constant zero,

`float0` is the sole element of a zero-dimensional vector space. Constant zero is a particular value within a 1-dimensional vector space.

No, `float0` arrays can have arbitrary shape. Each element in a `float0` array represents the sole element in a zero-dimensional vector space.

For example:
```python
In [2]: f0 = jax.vmap(jax.grad(jnp.float32, allow_int=True))(jax.numpy.arange(4))

In [3]: print(f0.shape, f0.dtype)
(4,) [('float0', 'V')]
```
This is a length 4 array of gradients with respect to integer inputs, each of which is a float0 value.
Reopening, we fixed the initial issue, but we need to think about the fact that `jax.jit(lambda x: x.imag.shape)(1.0)` fails for weakly-typed scalar inputs. It's a strange corner case...
Closing in deference to new, more succinct issue: https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/issues/27545

issue.body:
### Description
The following:
```python
import jax.numpy as jnp
from jax.lax import while_loop
from array_api_compat import get_namespace

def body(x):
    assert False

def cond(x):
    # x is a tracer, x.real is a tracer, x.imag is a float!
    xp = get_namespace(x)
    xp.square(x.imag)  # No problem with x.real!

while_loop(cond, body, jnp.asarray(0.0))
```
crashes with:
```
ValueError: square: inputs must be arrays; got types [<class 'float'>]
```

Also broken:
```python
import jax.numpy as jnp
from jax import jit

@jit
def f(x):
    x.imag.shape  # Crash!

f(jnp.asarray(0.0))
```
According to the Array API spec, `x.imag` must be a _Jax array_ (not a NumPy array, nor a float).

### System info (python version, jaxlib version, accelerator, etc.)

An NVIDIA GPU may be present on this machine, but a CUDA-enabled jaxlib is not installed. Falling back to cpu.
jax:    0.4.26
jaxlib: 0.4.26
numpy:  1.26.4
python: 3.11.8 (main, Feb 22 2024, 17:25:49) [GCC 11.4.0]

issue.title: [Reproduce] Bug #20624 - Jax

issue.body:
### Description

```python
import jax
import jax.numpy as jnp

def bar(x):
    return jnp.array(1), x + 1

def foo(x):
   x, y = jax.jit(bar, inline=True)(x)
   x.shape

jax.jit(foo)(0)
```
```
AttributeError: 'int' object has no attribute 'shape'
```
Expected behaviour is no error. Setting `inline=False` removes the error.
